title: PySpark Error Converting Irregular Date String to Timestamp Format
question:
I'm trying to convert irregular datetime string in my PySpark Dataframe to proper timestamp. The column value looks like this:

+------------------------------+
|date_added                    |
+------------------------------+
|Fri Aug 25 13:55:02 -0700 2017|
|Sun Jul 30 07:44:10 -0700 2017|
|Mon Jul 24 02:48:17 -0700 2017|
|Mon Jul 24 02:33:09 -0700 2017|
|Mon Jul 24 02:28:14 -0700 2017|
+------------------------------+

I've used to_timestamp() function with the following line of code below:

from pyspark.sql.functions import to_timestamp

format_str = "EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy"

df = df.withColumn("date_added", to_timestamp("date_added", format_str))

I also tried alternate patterns like:

"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss XXX yyyy"

"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss XX yyyy"

"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss z yyyy"

But I'm running into this error:

Traceback (most recent call last):                                              
  File "/etl_pipeline.py", line 111, in <module>
    reviews_df = transform_data(reviews_df)
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/etl_pipeline.py", line 86, in transform_data
    reviews_transformed_df.show(5)
  File "/miniconda3/envs/myenv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pyspark/sql/dataframe.py", line 947, in show
    print(self._show_string(n, truncate, vertical))
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/miniconda3/envs/myenv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pyspark/sql/dataframe.py", line 965, in _show_string
    return self._jdf.showString(n, 20, vertical)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/miniconda3/envs/myenv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/py4j/java_gateway.py", line 1322, in __call__
    return_value = get_return_value(
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/miniconda3/envs/myenv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pyspark/errors/exceptions/captured.py", line 185, in deco raise converted from None
pyspark.errors.exceptions.captured.SparkUpgradeException: [INCONSISTENT_BEHAVIOR_CROSS_VERSION.DATETIME_PATTERN_RECOGNITION] 
You may get a different result due to the upgrading to Spark >= 3.0:
Fail to recognize 'EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy' pattern in the DateTimeFormatter. 
1) You can set "spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy" to "LEGACY" to restore the behavior before Spark 3.0. 
2) You can form a valid datetime pattern with the guide from 'https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-ref-datetime-pattern.html'.

Setting spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy = LEGACY might does fix it, but I'd prefer a more future-proof solution if possible.

I don't want to use the legacy parser (spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy = LEGACY) unless there's absolutely no choice. How can I correctly parse this datetime string in PySpark 3.5.2?

Any help in forming a correct DateTimeFormatter pattern or preprocessing steps would be appreciated!
answer:
EEE is the offending part that is requiring the LEGACY and since this part is not necessary to convert to a timestamp, you could substring to remove first 4 characters and convert without EEE.

# substring 100 is large enough number to capture rest of the characters.   
format_str = "MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy"
df.withColumn('date_added', to_timestamp(substring("date_added", 5, 100), format_str))
